lede: The biggest thing on the government calendar this week is Mountain Village Town Council's first reading of an ordinance that would move Housing Authority fees out of municipal code and into an annually updated fee schedule — a structural shift worth understanding before it advances. Alongside that, the Housing Authority Subcommittee is wrestling with how to handle subpar bedrooms in mitigation units, the county's Housing Code Update working group continues its Prop 123-funded effort to clear land-use barriers, and HARC takes up a potential demolition and rebuild of Rebekah Hall — the very building where the commission meets.

notable.stake: Policy on subpar mitigation-unit bedrooms could affect housing stock quality and compliance.
Prop 123-funded code changes could reshape how affordable housing gets approved countywide.
Potential demolition of Town-owned Rebekah Hall is up for HARC work session review.
BOCC takes up view-plain MOU and constitutional amendment positions affecting county policy.
Two public hearings on new development and a subdivision in Ouray County — comment open.
First reading: ordinance shifting MVHA fees out of municipal code into adjustable fee schedule.
